messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated inference error rate detected on rollout 'release/v3' (canary nodes). Priority: P1. Affected customers: multiple hosted API tenants. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1815234000
Claire: I see the alert — can someone oncall confirm?
Jamal: oncall-ml here, looking. I can reproduce tokenization errors in the canary logs, lots of 'UnknownTokenSequence' exceptions.
Priya: tagging infra: did the deploy pipeline change tokenizer config?
Oscar: deploy-bot: pipeline started 3m ago: deploy/release-v3 -> model-serving:v3.0.1 + tokenizer-config update (tokenizer/v3-config.yaml).
Claire: Jamal, paste a log snippet?
Jamal: ``ERROR model_serving: tokenizer mismatch: expected vocab_size=50256, got=50290 at /app/tokenizer/load.py:78``
Jamal: Another one: ``Traceback (most recent call last): TokenizerError('mismatch in offsets')``
Priya: That sounds like a config drift — the tokenizer file in the artifact likely doesn't match the model weights. Could be packaging bug.
Oscar: Rolling canary only, but client-facing: we already routed 10% of requests. Need immediate mitigation.
Claire: Agreed. Options: 1) flip feature flag to stop routing to canary, 2) rollback to v2 stable, 3) disable tokenizer change via config kill flag if available. What's fastest?
oncall-ml: Quickest is toggling the canary routing flag to 0. I'll do that and monitor.
oncall-ml: /runops feature-flag set model_canary_route 0 --reason "tokenizer mismatch v3"
oncall-ml: deploy-bot: feature flag update accepted, routing at 0% for canary. Confirming traffic shift now.
incidents-bot: Traffic shift: canary->0%, stable->100% (3s). Error rate on public API decreasing.
Jamal: Error spikes dropping from 18% to 1.2% in the last 60s for user-facing requests.
Priya: Good. We should still assess whether any customers received malformed outputs. CS, please surface any immediate reports.
Claire: I'm going to open an incident ticket and start RCA notes.
Priya: Remote root cause hypothesis: tokenizer config packaged with v3 was from an intermediate branch (v3-tokenizer-experiment) and didn't match weights quantization/merging script. We should check build artifact provenance.
Oscar: I have the artifact hash: sha256:5f8b3a... checking CI logs for packaging step.
Jamal: Also found a few canary responses with truncated JSON from structured-output endpoints — likely tokenizer produced unexpected tokens that broke postprocessing.
Priya: Action items for now: (1) Keep canary traffic at 0, (2) Initiate rollback if any residual errors, (3) Validate artifact signing and CI job. Who owns rollback?
Claire: I'll take rollback coordination if we need it. Oscar, can you prepare a rollback image (v2.12.3)?
Oscar: prepared and standing by. rollback command: ``redwoodctl deploy rollback --service=model-serving --to=v2.12.3 --env=hosted --confirm``
Claire: I'll hold until we confirm no urgent customer incidents. Jamal, can you run a focused eval against a set of conserved prompts to check for any subtle regressions in the stable traffic?
Jamal: Running a 1000-prompt pass now against stable. ETA ~4m.
incidents-bot: Customer impact assessment: initial sampling shows ~12 unique request IDs returned malformed payloads during canary window. Most were from lower-traffic tenants; no major enterprise SLAs flagged yet.
Priya: Notify support to flag those tenants proactively. We should prepare an apology + explanation if they ask.
Claire: Support notified. Tagging: @support-team please see incident 1815234000, affected tenants list posted in incident ticket.
Jamal: 1000-prompt pass done. Stable results: 0 malformed outputs. Canary artifact (v3) local test reproduces tokenizer mismatch.
Oscar: CI confirmed: tokenizer config file for v3 in artifact was last modified by a branch merge 2h before deploy. The packaging step didn't assert vocab_size consistency. Adding fail-fast check to CI.
Priya: Good. After-action: enforce tokenizer metadata check (vocab_size, merges checksum) at packager and serving startup.
Claire: I'm going to keep this thread open and do a formal postmortem draft. For now incident state: mitigated (canary routing disabled), partial customer impact identified, no ongoing outage.
incidents-bot: Incident status changed to 'mitigated' at 1815234360. Pager cleared.
Jamal: One more note — we need a kill-switch in runtime that rejects mismatched tokenizer/model pairs with a clear error code so downstream systems can degrade safely.
Priya: Adding that to backlog with priority P0 for safety-critical path.
Oscar: CI fix PR opened: #4523 (adds vocab_size assert and artifact provenance check).
Claire: Thanks all. I'll run handoff to next oncall in ~10m and merge the PM/eng action items into the ticket. If anyone sees new customer reports, post them here.
oncall-ml: Handoff completed to Jamal for next 2h window.
incidents-bot: Incident closed at 1815234600 (post-mitigated monitoring).
